newsitem.title: USA: U.S. crude losses accumulate, grades remain steady.
newsitem.headline: U.S. crude losses accumulate, grades remain steady.

text.p: Cash crude prices in the U.S. Gulf lost ground Wednesday, declining to new session lows for outright prices, while grades wavered around steady levels.
August West Texas Intermediate/Cushing stood around 15 cents lower at $19.45-55 a barrel, and remained some 10-12 cents weaker than second month September contracts.

Cash dealers said the tone in the grade markets was steady and quiet, with most focus on new developments from Colombia, where force majeure declarations from Tuesday on Cano Limon production bolstered sour crude differentials.

The latest from Bogota had repairs starting later Wednesday on the dynamite-damaged Cano Limon-Covenas pipeline, the country's second largest line and the constant target of leftist National Liberation Army (ELN) bombings.
Occidental Petroleum Corp on Tuesday declared force majeure on Cano Limon field production, as a result of pipeline damage which has shut-in 180,000 barrels per day of production since July 6.

Colombian output concerns lifted the discount held by West Texas Sour/Midland barrels to around $1.05 on Tuesday, but the last trades on Wednesday saw WTS slip to $1.12 and $1.15 under August WTI/Cushing.
Grade talk had Light Louisiana Sweet/St. James at 23-25 cents over the marker, Heavy Louisiana Sweet/Empire at 35-30 cents under benchmark and Midland/WTI at 21-20 cents under.

Traders there was little momentum from refiners to move grade differentials sharply. "It's quiet out there and things really haven't changed all that much from Tuesday," said a cash dealer in the U.S. Gulf.
